title: ICE Agent Fatally Shoots Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston — Passengers Dispute DHS Account
detail: On July 7, 2026, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 52-year-old Mexican construction worker and father of three U.S.-citizen children who had lived in the U.S. for 35 years, was fatally shot by an ICE officer in Houston's Magnolia Park neighborhood while driving his construction crew to a job site. DHS said federal officers were looking for someone else when they attempted to stop his vehicle, and claimed Salgado Araujo rammed an ICE vehicle and refused commands to stop, prompting an officer to open fire in self-defense. Three passengers in the vehicle, who were detained by ICE, disputed that account through their attorney, saying the claim that Salgado Araujo tried to run over agents was false and that he had no criminal record and had begun applying for legal status. The Texas Rangers agreed to investigate alongside the FBI and DHS. The shooting immediately became a flashpoint in a broader pattern of fatal ICE enforcement encounters and prompted temporary reviews of ICE traffic-stop procedures.

title: GEO Group Settles Cal/OSHA Complaint for $100K+ Over Detainee Worker Safety at Golden State Annex
detail: GEO Group agreed to pay more than $100,000 to settle a landmark Cal/OSHA complaint over conditions at its Golden State Annex detention facility in McFarland, California, in a settlement signed in May and publicly announced July 7, 2026. California workplace safety inspectors opened the case in 2022 after complaints from advocates and detained immigrants working inside the facility's $1-a-day voluntary work program — covering tasks like cleaning, food preparation, and haircuts — alleging GEO failed to protect worker-detainees from COVID-19 spread and other hazards. As part of the settlement, GEO Group agreed to improve its disease-control plans and dropped its challenge to a prior state regulatory determination that the company is subject to California labor law — marking the first known instance of a state treating ICE detainees as employees and a detention operator as their employer under state labor statutes. GEO separately succeeded the prior month in getting ICE to update its own standards for detention contractors.
